# ARM MECHANICS EXTRACTION — what's usable vs. not

**Honesty note first:** Only 2 of your 7 images contain usable arm data (the manga how-to figure, the tameshigiri cutter, and the nukitsuke instruction photo). The rest are weapon-portrait/equipment shots with **zero arms**. I've extracted everything measurable and flagged estimates.

---

## 1) READY/IDLE STANCE (only source: image 2, manga construction figure)

Side-3/4 view, sword sheathed at left hip, right hand reaching to tsuka.

| Joint | R ARM (sword hand) | L ARM (saya hand) |
|---|---|---|
| Shoulder swing (0° = hanging straight down, + = forward) | +55° (upper arm raised forward to reach across to hip) | +10° |
| Shoulder abduction (out from torso) | ~15° | ~5° |
| Elbow interior flexion | ~100° (forearm angles sharply inward/down toward grip) | ~150° (nearly straight, hand resting on saya/koiguchi) |
| Wrist angle (neutral = 0°, + = dorsiflexed toward blade edge) | +20° (hand cocked to wrap tsuka) | ~0° |
| Hand height | At hip level / top of saya (≈ navel height, same Y as belt knot) | On saya mouth (koiguchi), slightly forward of hip |
| Lead hand | **RIGHT** (on tsuka, fingers visibly wrapping, thumb not locked) | Left trails, palm-down on scabbard |

**Tip the figure itself gives:** the scabbard must angle forward-down from the hip (~30–40° below horizontal) so the draw arcs *around* the body, not through it — keep the left-hand/saya anchor fixed while the right hand travels.

## 2) NUKITSUKE / DRAW (image 6 inset, plus image 5 follow-through)

### Keyframe table — right arm, side view:

| Phase | Shoulder swing | Elbow flexion | Wrist | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0. Grip rest | +55° | 100° | +20° | Left hand clamps saya forward |
| 1. Saya pull-back (sayabiki) | +45° | 110° | +20° | LEFT arm pulls saya back −15°, torso rotates |
| 2. Blade clears koiguchi | +70° | 130° | +40° | Right elbow extends outward; cut is horizontal, wrist cocked edge-up then snapping edge-down |
| 3. Cut extends (kiritsuke) | +85–90° | 165° | 0° | Arm nearly fully extended at chest height, blade horizontal |
| 4. Follow-through / chiburi (image 5) | +95° | 160° | −15° | Both hands stacked forward-low after the strike — see below |

## 3) OFF-HAND / TWO-HANDED GRIP (image 5 = post-cut, image 6 = one-handed phase)

| Phase | Left hand position |
|---|---|
| Sheathed | On saya, at koiguchi, palm down, elbow ~150° |
| Mid-draw | Releases saya, moves forward to meet tsuka **only after blade clears** |
| Two-handed (image 5) | Stacked: left hand at the **kashira (pommel end)**, right hand at fuchi/above tsuba; left pinky overhangs or cups kashira; wrists both near-neutral (±5°); hands at navel height, elbows flexed ~135°, pointing down-out |

---

## NOT USABLE (excluded per your instruction)
- Images 1, 3, 4: blade/koshirae dimensions only — no arms (useful only if you later want grip length: tsuka ≈ 23–33 cm per the diagrams).
- Image 7: arms occluded by wind-up pose; the leading arm shows shoulder ≈ +80°, elbow ~140° with weapon reversed-grip — usable only as a stylized dash reference.

**Implementation constants:** elbow flexion range never drops below ~95° while sheathed; full extension (~165–170°) only during cut; left arm stays within +10° to +45° shoulder swing the entire sequence; all wrist rotation happens in phase 2→3, not before.
message.reasoning_content: Only image 2 (figure pose) and 5, 6 show arms. Be honest about sparse data; estimate angles.
